subject: Pilot economics & ops checkpoints
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Klein <sam.klein@finteq.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot economics & ops checkpoints

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope and cost expectations: 

Pain points you shared
- Latency spikes on peak traffic (esp. fraud-check flows at 95th pct) leading to consumer checkout failures
- Token spend and per-transaction cost baked into current LLM validation pipeline is ~3–4x higher than product target
- Current infra is heterogeneous (on-prem for PII, GCP for inference) and you want predictable unit economics before committing to a pilot

What success looks like (your words)
- Reduce per-transaction inference cost by at least 40% while keeping 95th pct latency < 220ms
- Clear rollback plan and SLA for degradation modes (fallback model / queueing)
- Pilot that mirrors production topology (VPC + hybrid clouds) so the economics scale

Technical notes we captured
- Current stack: in-house Flask service -> K8s on GCP -> custom caching layer -> LLM calls to vendor X (batching minimal today)
- Average request: 320 tokens per validation, but median is ~120 tokens; peak concurrency ~420 qps for the endpoint
- Data constraints: PII never leaves your VPC; only tokenized embeddings can be cached in Redis (encrypted)

Our initial recommendations for the pilot (to validate unit economics)
1) Focused pilot on the fraud-validate path (5–7 day steady-state window) to measure per-transaction token cost and latency distribution
2) Enable prefix/KV caching plus continuous batching with a 25ms batching window to maximize throughput without violating 95th pct SLOs
3) Evaluate 4-bit quantized variant + fallback FP16 model for quality checks (you were open to quantization but want a brief eval)
4) Instrument token-level cost telemetry and a small prompt suite for quality regression monitoring

Next steps I propose
- I will send a short SOW + estimate and a proposed runbook for the 5–7 day pilot (attached).
- Action: Rishi to share a short anonymized sample trace (no PII) so we can size batching and cache hit expectations.
- Action: Sam to confirm legal/ops lead who will review VPC access and KMS requirements.

Can we target Wed 4/14 for Rishi + Sam to complete the sample trace and for me to send the SOW? If that works I can loop in solutions engineering for a short tech-run call.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

[Attachment: pilot_scope_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Sam Klein <sam.klein@finteq.io>

Cc: ops@finteq.io
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot economics & ops checkpoints

Aisha —

Appreciate the concise recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) When you say 25ms batching window, is that an upper bound or target? We can tolerate up to ~40ms on average as long as 95th pct stays under 220ms.
2) For quantization: we're interested but concerned about hallucination risk on our fraud prompts. We'll want to run your quality suite and a short human spot-check.
3) Sample trace: we can produce a sanitized trace by EOD Wed (4/14). Ops is copying in this thread.

Legal/ops lead: Laura Chen (laura.chen@finteq.io) will be the reviewer for VPC/KMS questions — she'll reach out if there are gating items.

For the SOW, please include an itemized pricing estimate for: dedicated reserved capacity vs. hosted + burst, and a line for engineering hours for integration support.

Best,
Sam
Head of Platform Engineering, Finteq
